sanskrit: tatas tu devavacanān maṇibhadro mahāyaśāḥ uvāca patitaṃ bhūmau kuṇḍadhāra kim iṣyate
english: Then, at the bidding of the gods, the greatly renowned Maṇibhadra spoke to Kuṇḍadhāra, who had fallen to the ground: "What is it that you desire?"

sanskrit: kuṇḍadhāra uvāca yadi prasannā devā me bhakto 'yaṃ brāhmaṇo mama asyānugraham icchāmi kṛtaṃ kiṃ cit sukhodayam
english: Kuṇḍadhāra said: "If the gods are gracious to me, this brāhmaṇa is my devotee. I wish that some favor be granted him from which his happiness may arise."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tatas taṃ maṇibhadras tu punar vacanam abravīt devānām eva vacanāt kuṇḍadhāraṃ mahādyutim
english: Bhīṣma said: Then Maṇibhadra, at the very word of the gods, spoke once more to the radiant Kuṇḍadhāra.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhadraṃ te kṛtakāryaḥ sukhī bhava yāvad dhanaṃ prārthayate brāhmaṇo 'yaṃ sakhā tava devānāṃ śāsanāt tāvad asaṃkhyeyaṃ dadāmy aham
english: "Rise up, rise up, good fortune to you! Your purpose is accomplished; be happy. However much wealth this brāhmaṇa, your friend, may ask for, that much—beyond counting—I shall give him, by the command of the gods."

sanskrit: vicārya kuṇḍadhāras tu mānuṣyaṃ calam adhruvam tapase matim ādhatta brāhmaṇasya yaśasvinaḥ
english: But Kuṇḍadhāra, reflecting that the human estate is unsteady and impermanent, turned his mind toward austerity for the illustrious brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: kuṇḍadhāra uvāca nāhaṃ dhanāni yācāmi brāhmaṇāya dhanaprada anyam evāham icchāmi bhaktāyānugrahaṃ kṛtam
english: Kuṇḍadhāra said: "I do not ask riches for the brāhmaṇa, O giver of wealth. Quite another favor is what I wish to have granted to my devotee."

sanskrit: pṛthivīṃ ratnapūrṇāṃ vā mahad vā dhanasaṃcayam bhaktāya nāham icchāmi bhaved eṣa tu dhārmikaḥ
english: "Not the earth filled with jewels, nor a vast hoard of wealth, do I wish for my devotee—rather, that he may become a man devoted to dharma."

sanskrit: dharme 'sya ramatāṃ buddhir dharmaṃ caivopajīvatu dharmapradhāno bhavatu mamaiṣo 'nugraho mataḥ
english: "Let his mind delight in dharma; let him live by dharma; let him hold dharma foremost. This is the favor I have in mind."

sanskrit: maṇibhadra uvāca yadā dharmaphalaṃ rājyaṃ sukhāni vividhāni ca phalāny evāyam aśnātu kāyakleśavivarjitaḥ
english: Maṇibhadra said: "Since sovereignty and manifold joys are the fruit of dharma, let him too partake of these fruits, freed from bodily affliction."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tatas tad eva bahuśaḥ kuṇḍadhāro mahāyaśāḥ abhyāsam akarod dharme tatas tuṣṭāsya devatāḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the greatly renowned Kuṇḍadhāra applied himself again and again to this very thing—the practice of dharma—and thereupon the gods were pleased with him.

sanskrit: maṇibhadra uvāca prītās te devatāḥ sarvā dvijasyāsya tathaiva ca bhaviṣyaty eṣa dharmātmā dharme cādhāsyate matiḥ
english: Maṇibhadra said: "All those gods are pleased with you, and likewise with this brāhmaṇa. He shall become a man whose very self is dharma, and he shall fix his mind upon dharma."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tataḥ prīto jaladharaḥ kṛtakāryo yudhiṣṭhira īpsitaṃ manaso labdhvā varam anyaiḥ sudurlabham
english: Bhīṣma said: Then Kuṇḍadhāra the cloud-bearer was glad, his purpose accomplished, O Yudhiṣṭhira, having obtained the boon his heart desired—one most hard for others to win.

sanskrit: tato 'paśyata cīrāṇi sūkṣmāṇi dvijasattamaḥ pārśvato 'bhyāgato nyastāny atha nirvedam āgataḥ
english: Then that best of brāhmaṇas saw fine bark garments laid down at his side, brought to him there; and he was overcome with world-weariness.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca ayaṃ na sukṛtaṃ vetti ko nv anyo vetsyate kṛtam gacchāmi vanam evāhaṃ varaṃ dharmeṇa jīvitum
english: The brāhmaṇa said: "This one does not know a good deed done him—who else, then, will recognize what is done for him? I shall go to the forest; better to live by dharma."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca nirvedād devatānāṃ ca prasādāt sa dvijottamaḥ vanaṃ praviśya sumahat tapa ārabdhavāṃs tadā
english: Bhīṣma said: Out of world-weariness, and by the grace of the gods, that best of brāhmaṇas entered the forest and there began a mighty austerity.

sanskrit: devatātithiśeṣeṇa phalamūlāśano dvijaḥ dharme cāpi mahārāja ratir asyābhyajāyata
english: Living on fruits and roots—on what was left after the gods and guests were served—that brāhmaṇa, O great king, came to find his delight in dharma.

sanskrit: tyaktvā mūlaphalaṃ sarvaṃ parṇāhāro 'bhavad dvijaḥ parṇaṃ tyaktvā jalāhāras tadāsīd dvijasattamaḥ
english: Giving up all roots and fruits, that brāhmaṇa became one who fed on leaves; and giving up leaves, that best of brāhmaṇas then subsisted on water alone.

sanskrit: vāyubhakṣas tataḥ paścād bahūn varṣagaṇān abhūt na cāsya kṣīyate prāṇas tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Thereafter, for many gatherings of years, he lived on air alone; and yet his life-breath did not waste away—and this was as a wonder.

sanskrit: dharme ca śraddadhānasya tapasy ugre ca vartataḥ kālena mahatā tasya divyā dṛṣṭir ajāyata
english: As he held faith in dharma and abided in fierce austerity, after a long span of time divine sight arose in him.

sanskrit: tasya buddhiḥ prādurāsīd yadi dadyāṃ mahad dhanam tuṣṭaḥ kasmai cid evāhaṃ na mithyā vāg bhaven mama
english: This thought arose in him: "Were I, well pleased, to bestow great wealth on anyone, my word would not prove false."

sanskrit: tataḥ prahṛṣṭavadano bhūya ārabdhavāṃs tapaḥ bhūyaś cācintayat siddho yat paraṃ so 'bhyapadyata
english: Then, his face joyful, he took up austerity once more; and the perfected one pondered again, and attained that which is higher still.

sanskrit: yadi dadyām ahaṃ rājyaṃ tuṣṭo vai yasya kasya cit sa bhaved acirād rājā na mithyā vāg bhaven mama
english: "Were I, well pleased, to bestow a kingdom upon anyone whatsoever, he would shortly become a king, and my word would not prove false."

sanskrit: tasya sākṣāt kuṇḍadhāro darśayām āsa bhārata brāhmaṇasya tapoyogāt sauhṛdenābhicoditaḥ
english: To him, O Bhārata, Kuṇḍadhāra showed himself in person, drawn by the power of the brāhmaṇa's austerity and moved by friendship.

sanskrit: samāgamya sa tenātha pūjāṃ cakre yathāvidhi brāhmaṇaḥ kuṇḍadhārasya vismitaś cābhavan nṛpa
english: Having met with him, the brāhmaṇa then did honor to Kuṇḍadhāra according to rite, and he was filled with wonder, O king.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīt kuṇḍadhāro divyaṃ te cakṣur uttamam paśya rājñāṃ gatiṃ vipra lokāṃś cāvekṣa cakṣuṣā
english: Then Kuṇḍadhāra said: "Yours is the supreme divine eye. Behold the destiny of kings, O wise one, and survey the worlds with that eye."

sanskrit: tato rājñāṃ sahasrāṇi magnāni niraye tadā dūrād apaśyad vipraḥ sa divyayuktena cakṣuṣā
english: Then that wise one, from afar, with the eye endowed with divine power, saw thousands of kings sunk down in hell.

sanskrit: kuṇḍadhāra uvāca māṃ pūjayitvā bhāvena yadi tvaṃ duḥkham āpnuyāḥ kṛtaṃ mayā bhavet kiṃ te kaś ca te 'nugraho bhavet
english: Kuṇḍadhāra said: "If, having honored me with true feeling, you were to come to grief, what would I have done for you, and what favor would have been yours?"

sanskrit: paśya paśya ca bhūyas tvaṃ kāmān icchet kathaṃ naraḥ svargadvāraṃ hi saṃruddhaṃ mānuṣeṣu viśeṣataḥ
english: "Look, look once more: how should a man crave the objects of desire? For the gate of heaven is barred shut—above all to mortals."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato 'paśyat sa kāmaṃ ca krodhaṃ lobhaṃ bhayaṃ madam nidrāṃ tandrīṃ tathālasyam āvṛtya puruṣān sthitān
english: Bhīṣma said: Then he beheld desire and anger, greed, fear, and intoxication, sleep, languor, and sloth standing there, enveloping men.

sanskrit: kuṇḍadhāra uvāca etair lokāḥ susaṃruddhā devānāṃ mānuṣād bhayam tathaiva devavacanād vighnaṃ kurvanti sarvaśaḥ
english: Kuṇḍadhāra said: "By these the worlds are tightly hemmed in. The gods fear mankind, and so, at the gods' word, these obstacles work hindrance in every way."

sanskrit: na devair ananujñātaḥ kaś cid bhavati dhārmikaḥ eṣa śakto 'si tapasā rājyaṃ dātuṃ dhanāni ca
english: "No one becomes righteous unless the gods permit it. Yet you, by your austerity, are now able to bestow a kingdom and riches."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tataḥ papāta śirasā brāhmaṇas toyadhāriṇe uvāca cainaṃ dharmātmā mahān me 'nugrahaḥ kṛtaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the brāhmaṇa, whose self was dharma, fell head-bowed before the cloud-bearer and said: "A great favor has been done me."

sanskrit: kāmalobhānubandhena purā te yad asūyitam mayā sneham avijñāya tatra me kṣantum arhasi
english: "For the grudging I once bore you, bound up with desire and greed, not knowing your affection—for that you ought to forgive me."

sanskrit: kṣāntam eva mayety uktvā kuṇḍadhāro dvijarṣabham saṃpariṣvajya bāhubhyāṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Saying "It is already forgiven by me," Kuṇḍadhāra embraced that bull among brāhmaṇas with both his arms and there and then vanished.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvān imāṃl lokān brāhmaṇo 'nucacāra ha kuṇḍadhāraprasādena tapasā yojitaḥ purā
english: Then the brāhmaṇa wandered through all these worlds, joined to such power of austerity, by the grace of Kuṇḍadhāra of old.

sanskrit: vihāyasā ca gamanaṃ tathā saṃkalpitārthatā dharmāc chaktyā tathā yogād yā caiva paramā gatiḥ
english: Travel through the sky, and the fulfillment of whatever he resolved upon—such power came to him from dharma and from yoga, and that supreme goal as well.

sanskrit: devatā brāhmaṇāḥ santo yakṣā mānuṣacāraṇāḥ dhārmikān pūjayantīha na dhanāḍhyān na kāminaḥ
english: Gods, brāhmaṇas, the good, yakṣas, men, and cāraṇas honor here the righteous—not the rich in wealth, nor the slaves of desire.

sanskrit: suprasannā hi te devā yat te dharme ratā matiḥ dhane sukhakalā kā cid dharme tu paramaṃ sukham
english: Truly the gods are well pleased that your mind delights in dharma. In wealth there is but some small fraction of joy, but in dharma is the supreme happiness.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca bahūnāṃ yajñatapasām ekārthānāṃ pitāmaha dharmārthaṃ na sukhārthārthaṃ kathaṃ yajñaḥ samāhitaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Of the many sacrifices and austerities that have one and the same aim, O grandfather, how was a sacrifice performed for the sake of dharma and not for the sake of pleasure?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atra te vartayiṣyāmi nāradenānukīrtitam uñchavṛtteḥ purāvṛttaṃ yajñārthe brāhmaṇasya ha
english: Bhīṣma said: On this I shall relate to you what was recounted by Nārada—an ancient tale of a gleaner-brāhmaṇa, concerning the matter of sacrifice.

sanskrit: rāṣṭre dharmottare śreṣṭhe vidarbheṣv abhavad dvijaḥ uñchavṛttir ṛṣiḥ kaś cid yajñe yajñaṃ samādadhe
english: In a most excellent realm rich in dharma, among the Vidarbhas, there once lived a brāhmaṇa, a certain sage who lived by gleaning, and he set about a sacrifice within his sacrifice.

sanskrit: śyāmākam aśanaṃ tatra sūryapatnī suvarcalā tiktaṃ ca virasaṃ śākaṃ tapasā svādutāṃ gatam
english: His food there was wild śyāmāka grain and suvarcalā, the consort of the Sun; and bitter, savorless greens, which by his austerity had turned sweet.

sanskrit: upagamya vane pṛthvīṃ sarvabhūtavihiṃsayā api mūlaphalair ijyo yajñaḥ svargyaḥ paraṃtapa
english: Resorting to the earth in the forest, without harm to any living being, a sacrifice offered even with roots and fruits leads to heaven, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: tasya bhāryā vratakṛśā śuciḥ puṣkaracāriṇī yajñapatnītvam ānītā satyenānuvidhīyate sā tu śāpaparitrastā na svabhāvānuvartinī
english: His wife, gaunt with vows, pure, who moved among the lotus-pools, had been brought to the office of sacrificer's wife; by truth she was made to comply—yet she, terrified of a curse, did not act according to her own nature.

sanskrit: mayūrajīrṇaparṇānāṃ vastraṃ tasyāś ca parṇinām akāmāyāḥ kṛtaṃ tatra yajñe hotrānumārgataḥ
english: A garment of peacock-feathers and worn leaves was made for her, leaf-clad as she was and unwilling, there at the sacrifice, in accordance with the office of the hotṛ.

sanskrit: śukrasya punar ājātir apadhyānād adharmavit tasmin vane samīpastho mṛgo 'bhūt sahacārikaḥ vacobhir abravīt satyaṃ tvayā duṣkṛtakaṃ kṛtam
english: Now a rebirth of Śukra, fallen through wrong meditation and unversed in dharma, had become in that forest a deer dwelling nearby, a companion; and with words it spoke the truth: "An ill deed has been done by you."

sanskrit: yadi mantrāṅgahīno 'yaṃ yajño bhavati vaikṛtaḥ māṃ bhoḥ prakṣipa hotre tvaṃ gaccha svargam atandritaḥ
english: "If this sacrifice is marred, lacking in mantras and ritual limbs—then cast me, sir, into the offering, and go untiring to heaven."

sanskrit: tatas tu yajñe sāvitrī sākṣāt taṃ saṃnyamantrayat nimantrayantī pratyuktā na hanyāṃ sahavāsinam
english: Then at the sacrifice Sāvitrī in person summoned him; but when she invited him, he answered: "I will not slay one who dwells beside me."

sanskrit: evam uktā nivṛttā sā praviṣṭā yajñapāvakam kiṃ nu duścaritaṃ yajñe didṛkṣuḥ sā rasātalam
english: Thus answered, she turned back and entered the sacrificial fire—wishing to see what wrong there might be in the sacrifice, even down to the nether world.

sanskrit: sā tu baddhāñjaliṃ satyam ayācad dhariṇaṃ punaḥ satyena saṃpariṣvajya saṃdiṣṭo gamyatām iti
english: Then she, with hands joined in entreaty, again besought the deer by truth; and embracing it with truth, she enjoined: "Let it be permitted to go."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa hariṇo gatvā padāny aṣṭau nyavartata sādhu hiṃsaya māṃ satya hato yāsyāmi sadgatim
english: Then that deer, having gone eight steps, turned back: "Slay me freely, O truthful one; slain, I shall go to a good destiny."

sanskrit: paśya hy apsaraso divyā mayā dattena cakṣuṣā vimānāni vicitrāṇi gandharvāṇāṃ mahātmanām
english: "Behold the divine apsarases—with the eye I have given you—and the wondrous chariots of the great-souled gandharvas."

sanskrit: tataḥ suruciraṃ dṛṣṭvā spṛhālagnena cakṣuṣā mṛgam ālokya hiṃsāyāṃ svargavāsaṃ samarthayat
english: Then, beholding that lovely sight with an eye fixed in longing, and gazing upon the deer, he deemed dwelling in heaven worth the act of killing.

sanskrit: sa tu dharmo mṛgo bhūtvā bahuvarṣoṣito vane tasya niṣkṛtim ādhatta na hy asau yajñasaṃvidhiḥ
english: But it was Dharma who, having become a deer, dwelt many years in the forest; he set in train the man's expiation—for that was no proper rule of sacrifice.

sanskrit: tasya tena tu bhāvena mṛgahiṃsātmanas tadā tapo mahat samucchinnaṃ tasmād dhiṃsā na yajñiyā
english: By that very intent—his mind bent on slaying the deer—his great austerity was then cut off; therefore killing is not fit for sacrifice.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ bhagavān dharmo yajñaṃ yājayata svayam samādhānaṃ ca bhāryāyā lebhe sa tapasā param
english: Then the lord Dharma himself caused him to perform the sacrifice; and by his austerity he gained the supreme reconciliation of his wife.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā sakalo dharmo hiṃsā yajñe 'samāhitā satyaṃ te 'haṃ pravakṣyāmi yo dharmaḥ satyavādinām
english: Non-injury is the whole of dharma; injury in sacrifice is unfitting. I shall declare to you the truth—what is the dharma of those who speak the truth.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ bhavati pāpātmā kathaṃ dharmaṃ karoti vā kena nirvedam ādatte mokṣaṃ vā kena gacchati
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How does a man become evil-souled, and how does he do what is righteous? By what does he take up world-weariness, and by what does he attain liberation?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca viditāḥ sarvadharmās te sthityartham anupṛcchasi śṛṇu mokṣaṃ sanirvedaṃ pāpaṃ dharmaṃ ca mūlataḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: All the dharmas are known to you; you ask for the sake of confirming them. Hear of liberation together with world-weariness, and of evil and of dharma, from their very root.

sanskrit: vijñānārthaṃ hi pañcānām icchā pūrvaṃ pravartate prāpya tāñ jāyate kāmo dveṣo vā bharatarṣabha
english: For the sake of perceiving the objects of the five senses, desire first sets to work; and on attaining them, craving or aversion is born, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tatas tadarthaṃ yatate karma cārabhate punaḥ iṣṭānāṃ rūpagandhānām abhyāsaṃ ca cikīrṣati
english: Then for the sake of that he strives, and undertakes action anew, and seeks to make a habit of the pleasing forms and scents he loves.

sanskrit: tato rāgaḥ prabhavati dveṣaś ca tadanantaram tato lobhaḥ prabhavati mohaś ca tadanantaram
english: From that, passion arises, and aversion straight after; from that, greed arises, and delusion straight after.

sanskrit: lobhamohābhibhūtasya rāgadveṣānvitasya ca na dharme jāyate buddhir vyājād dharmaṃ karoti ca
english: In one overwhelmed by greed and delusion, beset by passion and aversion, no true mind for dharma is born; and he practices dharma only as a pretext.

sanskrit: vyājena carato dharmam arthavyājo 'pi rocate vyājena sidhyamāneṣu dhaneṣu kurunandana
english: To one who practices dharma as a mere pretext, the pretext of gain too becomes pleasing, as riches are won through such pretense, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: tatraiva kurute buddhiṃ tataḥ pāpaṃ cikīrṣati suhṛdbhir vāryamāṇo 'pi paṇḍitaiś cāpi bhārata
english: On that very thing he sets his mind, and then he seeks to do evil, even though restrained by his friends and by the wise, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: uttaraṃ nyāyasaṃbaddhaṃ bravīti vidhiyojitam adharmas trividhas tasya vardhate rāgamohajaḥ
english: He gives a rejoinder cloaked in reason and dressed up in scripture; and his unrighteousness, born of passion and delusion, grows threefold.

sanskrit: pāpaṃ cintayate caiva prabravīti karoti ca tasyādharmapravṛttasya doṣān paśyanti sādhavaḥ
english: He thinks evil, and speaks it, and does it; and the good perceive the faults of him who is bent upon unrighteousness.

sanskrit: ekaśīlāś ca mitratvaṃ bhajante pāpakarmiṇaḥ sa neha sukham āpnoti kuta eva paratra vai
english: Only those of like character take up friendship with the evildoer. He gains no happiness here—how then could he hereafter?

sanskrit: evaṃ bhavati pāpātmā dharmātmānaṃ tu me śṛṇu yathā kuśaladharmā sa kuśalaṃ pratipadyate
english: Thus a man becomes evil-souled. Now hear from me of the righteous-souled—how one whose dharma is wholesome attains to the wholesome.

sanskrit: ya etān prajñayā doṣān pūrvam evānupaśyati kuśalaḥ sukhaduḥkhānāṃ sādhūṃś cāpy upasevate
english: He who, with discernment, foresees these faults beforehand—skilled in the ways of pleasure and pain—attends as well upon the good.

sanskrit: tasya sādhusamācārād abhyāsāc caiva vardhate prajñā dharme ca ramate dharmaṃ caivopajīvati
english: From his good conduct and from constant practice his wisdom grows; he delights in dharma and lives by dharma.

sanskrit: so 'tha dharmād avāpteṣu dhaneṣu kurute manaḥ tasyaiva siñcate mūlaṃ guṇān paśyati yatra vai
english: Then, upon the riches won through dharma, he sets his mind; he waters the very root of that whence he sees virtues arise.

sanskrit: dharmātmā bhavati hy evaṃ mitraṃ ca labhate śubham sa mitradhanalābhāt tu pretya ceha ca nandati
english: Thus he becomes righteous-souled and gains a worthy friend; and through the gaining of friends and wealth he rejoices both hereafter and here.

sanskrit: śabde sparśe tathā rūpe rase gandhe ca bhārata prabhutvaṃ labhate jantur dharmasyaitat phalaṃ viduḥ
english: In sound and touch, in form, taste, and scent, O Bhārata, the creature gains mastery; this they know to be the fruit of dharma.

sanskrit: sa dharmasya phalaṃ labdhvā na tṛpyati yudhiṣṭhira atṛpyamāṇo nirvedam ādatte jñānacakṣuṣā
english: Having won the fruit of dharma, he is not sated, O Yudhiṣṭhira; and unsated, with the eye of knowledge, he takes up world-weariness.

sanskrit: prajñācakṣur yadā kāme doṣam evānupaśyati virajyate tadā kāmān na ca dharmaṃ vimuñcati
english: When, with the eye of wisdom, he perceives the fault in desire, then he turns away from desires, yet does not let go of dharma.

sanskrit: sarvatyāge ca yatate dṛṣṭvā lokaṃ kṣayātmakam tato mokṣāya yatate nānupāyād upāyataḥ
english: Seeing the world to be of the nature of decay, he strives for total renunciation; thereafter he strives for liberation—not by wrong means, but by right ones.

sanskrit: śanair nirvedam ādatte pāpaṃ karma jahāti ca dharmātmā caiva bhavati mokṣaṃ ca labhate param
english: Little by little he takes up world-weariness and casts off evil deeds; he becomes righteous-souled and attains the supreme liberation.

sanskrit: etat te kathitaṃ tāta yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi pāpaṃ dharmaṃ tathā mokṣaṃ nirvedaṃ caiva bhārata
english: This I have told you, my son, that which you asked of me—evil, and dharma, and liberation, and world-weariness, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tasmād dharme pravartethāḥ sarvāvasthaṃ yudhiṣṭhira dharme sthitānāṃ kaunteya siddhir bhavati śāśvatī
english: Therefore set yourself to dharma in every condition, O Yudhiṣṭhira; for those who stand firm in dharma, O son of Kuntī, attainment is everlasting.
